questions.topic: ETL vs ELT: Where Transformation Lives
questions.question: What is the defining architectural difference between ETL and ELT?
options: Whether transformation runs on a separate processing tier before loading, or inside the warehouse after loading
Whether the pipeline moves data in scheduled batches or as a continuously running stream of events
Whether the source systems are relational databases or semi-structured event logs and API feeds
Whether the loading step is performed by managed cloud services or by self-hosted worker machines

questions.topic: ETL vs ELT: Where Transformation Lives
questions.question: Which economic shift made ELT a practical default for analytics platforms?
options: Source databases began exposing change logs that made extraction nearly free for consumers
Network bandwidth between data centers became fast enough to move raw data twice per day
Cloud warehouses separated cheap columnar storage from elastic pay-per-use query compute
Open-source schedulers made it cheap to coordinate many small transformation jobs at once

questions.topic: ETL vs ELT: Where Transformation Lives
questions.question: A compliance rule states that unmasked card numbers may never be stored anywhere in the analytics project. Which approach satisfies this?
options: Load raw payloads into a restricted dataset and run a masking SQL model within the hour
Mask the field in the processing tier during flight, so only masked data ever lands
Store raw payloads encrypted at rest and grant analysts access only to masked views
Keep raw payloads in a staging bucket with a short lifecycle rule that deletes them daily

questions.topic: ETL vs ELT: Where Transformation Lives
questions.question: Weeks after launch, a team learns their parser dropped orders with multi-currency line items. Under which design can they recover the lost rows without going back to the source system?
options: An ETL design, because the processing tier keeps in-memory copies of each batch it transformed
Either design, because warehouse time travel can restore any table to a prior snapshot state
An ETL design, because transformation failures there raise errors instead of loading bad rows
An ELT design, because the unparsed payloads were loaded first and are still queryable

questions.topic: ETL vs ELT: Where Transformation Lives
questions.question: An ELT team's warehouse bill spikes during development because engineers keep iterating on transformation SQL. What is the most likely cause and fix?
options: Scheduled models run too frequently; lowering the schedule to weekly will cut most of the cost
Dev queries repeatedly full-scan the large raw table; partition it and develop against samples
Raw storage is growing without bound; shortening raw retention will bring the bill back down
The warehouse caches too aggressively; disabling result caching will reduce compute charges

questions.topic: ETL vs ELT: Where Transformation Lives
questions.question: A pipeline must attach model-generated embeddings to each document before analysts can use them. Why does this push the design toward transformation outside the warehouse?
options: Embedding generation needs ML libraries and model inference that warehouse SQL cannot express
Embedding vectors are too wide to store in columnar formats used by analytical warehouses
Warehouses cannot schedule recurring transformations without an external orchestration tool
Loading documents before embedding them would violate schema-on-read storage conventions

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of the raw zone?
options: To hold per-run extraction batches until the loader verifies and promotes them downstream
To give analysts a low-latency workspace for exploratory queries against recent source data
To keep a permanent, append-only archive of data exactly as it arrived, enabling reprocessing
To store cleaned and conformed tables that dashboards and ML feature jobs read directly

questions.question: Which zone should dashboards, feature pipelines, and other consumers read from?
options: The staging zone, because it holds the freshest data available at any given moment
The raw zone, because it is the most complete and faithful record of the source
Whichever zone currently has the field they need for the analysis at hand
The curated zone, where data is deduplicated, typed, and modeled under stable schemas

questions.question: A transform bug has been corrupting a curated column for three weeks before anyone notices. What makes this recoverable rather than a permanent data loss?
options: The raw zone still holds every original payload, so the fixed transform can rebuild curated
The staging zone retains each load batch, so the affected weeks can be re-promoted from it
The curated zone is versioned by convention, so an earlier correct snapshot can be restored
The warehouse audit log records every mutation, so the bad writes can be reversed in place

questions.question: Which property correctly describes the staging zone?
options: It is append-only and immutable, holding history that downstream fixes will re-read for years
It is transient scaffolding, one batch per load run, safely truncated after promotion succeeds
It is the consumer-facing layer where business logic and naming standards are applied
It is a schema-enforced mirror of curated used to test transformations before release

questions.question: A GDPR erasure request must be honored, but the raw zone is immutable by convention. How do teams typically reconcile this?
options: Exclude raw from erasure obligations since it is an internal archive not served to users
Move affected users' rows to staging, which is transient and therefore exempt from requests
Delete the entire raw partition range containing the user and accept the collateral data loss
Rewrite the affected partitions or use per-user encryption keys that can be destroyed

questions.question: An analytics team starts querying the raw zone directly because curated lacks a field they need. What is the principled objection?
options: Raw queries bypass warehouse caching, so their dashboards will be slower and more expensive
Raw data is stored in formats that most business intelligence tools cannot connect to at all
They now depend on an uncontracted, unstable schema, and the fix is to promote the field into curated
They will see duplicate rows, and deduplicating in their own queries is too computationally costly

questions.topic: Data Contracts Between Producers and Consumers
questions.question: Beyond field names and types, what does a complete data contract specify?
options: Semantics such as units and timezones, SLAs for freshness, and rules for schema evolution
The storage format, compression codec, and partitioning layout of the producer's tables
The orchestration schedule, retry policy, and alerting channels for the ingestion pipeline
The access control roles and billing project under which consumers may query the data

questions.topic: Data Contracts Between Producers and Consumers
questions.question: Which schema change is backward compatible under a typical additive-only evolution rule?
options: Renaming `amount_cents` to `amount` while keeping the integer type unchanged
Changing `amount_cents` from an integer type to a string to support formatting
Adding a new optional, nullable field such as `discount_cents` to the event
Removing a field that telemetry shows no registered consumer has queried recently

questions.topic: Data Contracts Between Producers and Consumers
questions.question: A producer team renames a column during a refactor and downstream dashboards silently fill with nulls. Which safeguard would have caught this before any bad event was emitted?
options: A freshness SLA alert configured on the curated tables that the dashboards read from
A contract check in the producer's CI that blocks merges making breaking schema changes
A nightly reconciliation query comparing row counts between raw and curated zones
A quarantine rule at ingestion that diverts batches whose null rates exceed a threshold

questions.topic: Data Contracts Between Producers and Consumers
questions.question: At which two points is a data contract typically enforced by machinery rather than documentation?
options: In the warehouse query optimizer and in the business intelligence tool's semantic layer
In the curated zone's access controls and in the consumer team's dashboard definitions
In the orchestrator's DAG definition and in the warehouse's table description metadata
In the producer's CI on schema changes and at ingestion when batches are validated

questions.topic: Data Contracts Between Producers and Consumers
questions.question: A platform team cannot get producer teams to add contract checks to their CI yet. What is the pragmatic interim posture?
options: Pause new ingestion until every producer formally signs and enforces a contract document
Copy each producer's schema weekly into curated so consumers always match the source
Validate at ingestion, quarantine violating batches, and alert on drift without blocking producers
Accept all payloads into curated and rely on consumers to report anomalies as they appear

questions.topic: Data Contracts Between Producers and Consumers
questions.question: A genuinely breaking change to an event schema is unavoidable. What is the standard rollout that avoids a big-bang cutover?
options: Publish the new version alongside the old during a migration window, then retire the old version
Schedule a coordinated deploy where the producer and all consumers switch at the same instant
Apply the change directly and rely on ingestion quarantine to hold consumers' bad batches
Have consumers add defensive parsing for both shapes and leave the topic version unchanged
